greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who holds every moment of our lives in his hands, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the light that shines in the darkness: Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you invite us to trust in your eternal plan: Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you are the refuge of our souls in every age: Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: In every age, O Lord, you have been our refuge.
homily:
There is a particular kind of silence that settles over a house when the morning light first touches the windows. It is a quiet that is not empty; it is a quiet that is expectant. In the book of Ecclesiastes, we hear that ancient, rhythmic invitation: 'Rejoice, O young man, while you are young, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth.' It is a beautiful, piercing command. It asks us to look at the dawn, to look at the unfolding of a life, and to see it not as a fleeting thing to be mourned, but as a gift to be celebrated. 

I want you to think about the image of the 'silver cord' and the 'golden bowl' that the Scripture mentions today. These are fragile, beautiful things—the vessels that hold the essence of a life. When we think of Benjamin, we do not think of the breaking of the bowl. We think of the light it held. We think of a boy who, at fifteen, had already walked more of the world than most, a boy who stood under the vast sky of Tokyo, or in the quiet, sacred spaces of the Vatican, with a heart that was wide open to the horizon. 

Benjamin was a boy who looked at the world and saw potential. He didn't just see a plane; he saw 'con chim airlines.' He didn't just see a screen; he saw a place to build, to code, to create a future. He had that brilliant, analytical mind that could grasp the complexities of the world, but he carried it with the gentleness of a soul that knew the most important things in life are not the things we build, but the love we give. Think of that moment when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle. He didn't break it open. He didn't make a show of it. He simply offered. That is the heart of a saint. That is the heart that belongs to the Kingdom of Heaven.

But today, the Gospel gives us a moment that is, at first, very hard to hear. Jesus says to his disciples, 'Pay attention to what I am telling you. The Son of Man is to be handed over to men.' And the Scripture tells us something very human: 'they did not understand this saying; its meaning was hidden from them... and they were afraid to ask him.' 

How many of us have stood in that same place? We look at the events of our lives, the moments that change everything, and we are afraid to ask 'Why?' We are afraid because we fear the answer might be silence. We fear that if we ask, we will find that God is far away. But look closely at the disciples. They were afraid to ask, yet they remained with Him. They stayed in His presence. They kept walking the road, even when the path ahead was hidden in shadow. 

Alan and Thao, I know the weight of that silence. I know that three months have passed, and yet, in the quiet of the 3:00 a.m. hour, the heart still listens for a voice, still waits for the sound of a footstep in the hall. You have carried your love for Benjamin like a precious, glowing ember. You have kept his spirit alive in the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, in the kindness you show to others in his name, in the way you honor his memory as a family of four. You are doing exactly what the disciples did: you are staying with the Lord, even when you do not understand the path. You are not walking away. You are holding on. And in that holding on, you are being held.

Ryan, my dear brother, you are the one who knows the laughter best. You know the way Ben would giggle when he talked about his dreams. When you feel the loneliness, remember that you are not just a brother who is left behind. You are a brother who is walking forward with his heart inside your own. You are the one who keeps the dream of 'con chim airlines' alive in your own curiosity, in your own kindness. When you feel the world is quiet, know that you are never walking alone. You are the guardian of his memory, and you are the one who is showing the world what it looks like to love a brother with an eternal love.

There is a temptation to look back at the past and wonder if we missed a sign, or if we could have done more. I want to lift that stone from your hearts today. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the family he cherished. You did not miss anything. You are not being accused by God, and you must not accuse yourselves. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of 'what if.' That is a weight that belongs to the dust, and Christ has already stepped into the future to welcome Benjamin home. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

In the Psalm today, we pray: 'Teach us to number our days aright, that we may gain wisdom of heart.' This is not a call to count the days we have lost, but to cherish the days we have been given. Benjamin’s life was not a life that was 'cut short' in the eyes of God; it was a life that was completed in the light of His love. He lived with a brilliance that touched everyone he met. He was a boy who looked at the world with wonder, and now, he is looking at the face of the Creator. He is at the Banquet of Heaven, and he is cheering for you. He is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile, that same quiet, steady love.

I want you to think of the image of the 'well' again. A well is a place where we go to find what we need to live. The 'Well of Love' in Vietnam is a perfect symbol of Benjamin’s life. It is not a closed system; it is a source of life that keeps giving. His kindness, his empathy—the way he wanted to help his uncle, the way he loved his family—that love is still flowing. It is still quenching the thirst of the poor. It is still bringing hope to the weary. His life was a gift that continues to unfold. You are the stewards of that gift. Every act of kindness you do, every time you choose to love instead of despair, you are keeping his spirit alive and flowing into the world.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is a simple thing, but a profound one. When the weight of the silence feels too heavy, when the 'why' feels too big for your heart, do not look for answers in the past. Look for the presence in the 'Who.' When you see a plane in the sky, when you see a bird in flight, when you feel a sudden, warm memory of his smile, whisper his name, and then whisper the name of Jesus. Let those two names be your anchor. 

You are a family of four, and you are being led, step by step, through the darkness and into the light. The reunion is certain. And in the meantime, keep walking in the presence of God, in the light of the living. He is there, he is waiting, and he is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile. You are not walking alone. You are walking toward the Banquet, where all the laborers are gathered, where all the tears are wiped away, and where the love you shared will bloom forever. 

Let us not be afraid to ask, and let us not be afraid to hope. The meaning of the journey is hidden from us for now, but the Destination is clear. It is the heart of the Father. And Benjamin is already there, waiting for you, with his arms open wide. Live for him, yes, but live for the One who gave him to you, and who has now called him home. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when the evening comes, and you feel the weight of the day, remember the words of the Psalm: 'Fill us at daybreak with your kindness, that we may shout for joy and gladness all our days.' That joy is waiting for you. It is a promise, sealed in the heart of God, and it will never, ever fade. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may He let His face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may He give you His peace. Go in the peace of Christ.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin Vo and all who have gone before us, that they may rest forever in the light and peace of Christ, we pray to the Lord.
For all who are grieving, that God may console their hearts, strengthen their steps, and fill them with the hope of the Resurrection, we pray to the Lord.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
Rejoice, O young man, while you are young 
and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth.
Follow the ways of your heart,
the vision of your eyes;
Yet understand that as regards all this
God will bring you to judgment.
Ward off grief from your heart
and put away trouble from your presence,
though the dawn of youth is fleeting.Remember your Creator in the days of your youth,
before the evil days come
And the years approach of which you will say,
I have no pleasure in them;
Before the sun is darkened,
and the light, and the moon, and the stars,
while the clouds return after the rain;
When the guardians of the house tremble,
and the strong men are bent,
And the grinders are idle because they are few,
and they who look through the windows grow blind;
When the doors to the street are shut,
and the sound of the mill is low;
When one waits for the chirp of a bird,
but all the daughters of song are suppressed;
And one fears heights,
and perils in the street;
When the almond tree blooms,
and the locust grows sluggish
and the caper berry is without effect,
Because man goes to his lasting home,
and mourners go about the streets;
Before the silver cord is snapped
and the golden bowl is broken,
And the pitcher is shattered at the spring,
and the broken pulley falls into the well,
And the dust returns to the earth as it once was,
and the life breath returns to God who gave it.Vanity of vanities, says Qoheleth,
all things are vanity!

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (1) In every age, O Lord, you have been our refuge.
You turn man back to dust,
saying, “Return, O children of men.”
For a thousand years in your sight 
are as yesterday, now that it is past,
or as a watch of the night.
R. In every age, O Lord, you have been our refuge.
You make an end of them in their sleep;
the next morning they are like the changing grass,
Which at dawn springs up anew,
but by evening wilts and fades.
R. In every age, O Lord, you have been our refuge.
Teach us to number our days aright,
that we may gain wisdom of heart.
Return, O LORD! How long?
Have pity on your servants!
R. In every age, O Lord, you have been our refuge.
Fill us at daybreak with your kindness,
that we may shout for joy and gladness all our days.
And may the gracious care of the LORD our God be ours;
prosper the work of our hands for us!
Prosper the work of our hands!
R. In every age, O Lord, you have been our refuge.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
While they were all amazed at his every deed,
Jesus said to his disciples,
“Pay attention to what I am telling you.
The Son of Man is to be handed over to men.” 
But they did not understand this saying;
its meaning was hidden from them
so that they should not understand it,
and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.

day: Saturday of the Twenty-Fifth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.text: Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
Hey Ben,  nếu có thể hãy cho anh Minh gặp Ben trong giấc mơ nhé, dù chỉ là lời chào hay nụ cười như cách Ben vẫn hay tạo dáng để chụp hình. Nhớ và thương Ben nhiều lắm
